question: The Pakhawaj syllables are primarily used to conclude which of the following Indian classical dances?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Odissi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pakhawaj syllables** are rhythmically chanted as the dance gradually transitions from slow to rapid sequences, culminating in a climactic moment when the dancer offers their final respects.
 
• **An Odissi **ensemble typically comprises a pakhawaj player (often the Guru), a vocalist, a flautist, a sitar or violinist, and a manjira player.
 
• The dancer adorns themselves with intricate Odiya silver jewellery and a distinctive hairstyle. The saree, commonly tailored nowadays, is distinctive to the Odissi tradition.
 
• In each performance, even in modern Odissi dance, there is a reiteration of the spiritual quest for liberation or moksha, echoing the traditions of the devadasis and maharis who sought enlightenment through dance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] 

**Important Points__**

__
 
• **Odissi**, also known as Orissi in ancient texts, is a prominent classical dance form with roots tracing back to the temples of Odisha, a coastal state in eastern India. 
 
• Odissi was predominantly performed by female artists and served as a medium to convey religious narratives and spiritual concepts, particularly those associated with Vaishnavism. 
 
• These stories were conveyed through songs composed in accordance with the ragas and talas of Odissi music by poets from the region. 
 
• Additionally, Odissi performances often encompass themes from other traditions, including tales related to Hindu deities such as Shiva, Surya, and various Hindu goddesses associated with Shaktism. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Manipuri, **also known as the Manipuri Raas Leela, is a jagoi and counts among the prominent Indian classical dance styles, originating from the state of Manipur.
 
• **Kathak,** one of the eight principal Indian classical dances, traces its origins to the wandering minstrels of ancient northern India, known as Kathakars or storytellers.
 
• **Kathakali,** a traditional form of classical Indian dance, stands as one of the oldest theater forms still in practice. It falls into the category of "story game" artistry, distinguished by the intricately colorful makeup and costumes worn by the traditional male actor-dancers.
